reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that shot charts can be modeled as a marked spatial point process, where each shot is a point in space with an associated binary mark indicating success. The joint modeling approach uses a non-homogeneous Poisson process for shot locations and logistic regression for shot success. This allows for simultaneous inference on both spatial density and outcome probability. The intensity function λ(s) = exp(Z(s)^T α) encodes how shot frequency varies with spatial features such as distance or 3-point shot presence. Meanwhile, the mark model p(m=1|s) = sigmoid(X(s)^T β) captures conditional success probability. The spike-slab prior enables automatic variable selection, identifying which spatial features significantly influence either intensity or success. The MCMC sampling strategy using Gibbs and MH ensures convergence to posterior distributions. The dual nature of this model—spatial and probabilistic—enables GSI to compute shot likelihoods and GSE to simulate optimal positioning strategies.
